gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 12?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 12 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Ensemble spread remains narrow, though slight upward revisions could occur if steering patterns strengthen; traders are monitoring the next 00Z and 12Z model cycles for confirmation ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from European models indicate daytime maxima in Munich near 30–31 °C on August 13, with narrow spreads of 1–2 °C reflecting modest uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing and local advection. A broad ridge supporting subsidence and light easterly flow has sustained the warmth, while overnight radiative cooling keeps minima in the mid-teens. Historical August climatology centers on 24–25 °C highs, so the current setup represents a modest positive anomaly without extreme heatwave amplification. Trader consensus clusters on 30–31 °C because resolution hinges on the official DWD station reading, where small shifts in cloud cover or wind could tip the exact peak. Updated model runs and the final 24-hour guidance expected on August 12 remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover and widespread showers across the Tokyo region on August 12 are the dominant factors suppressing daytime heating, keeping the highest temperature centered on 27–28°C.** The Japan Meteorological Agency’s guidance explicitly forecasts a maximum near 28°C under these conditions, with extensive low-level clouds and precipitation limiting incoming solar radiation despite the seasonal background of above-normal warmth for mid-August. 

Ensemble forecast variability clusters tightly around this range because modest changes in shower timing or intensity can shift the peak by 1–2°C, while any prolonged drier breaks would be required to push readings to 29°C or higher. Historical August climatology in Tokyo shows typical highs near 31–32°C under clearer skies, but the current synoptic pattern—with its emphasis on moisture and reduced insolation—explains why traders assign the large majority of implied probability (over 89% combined) to the 27°C and 28°C outcomes. Updated model runs and official briefings through the morning of the 12th continue to reinforce this capped thermal profile.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent short-term forecast model consensus from agencies like the Japan Meteorological Agency points to partly cloudy conditions with isolated thunderstorms on August 14, moderating peak radiative heating and holding Tokyo's daily maximum near 28–29 °C. The strengthening Pacific High continues to advect warm, humid maritime air northward, sustaining urban heat-island amplification, yet increased cloud cover and potential afternoon convection are expected to cap extremes below historical mid-August averages. Ensemble guidance shows limited spread around these values, with slight downward revisions in the latest runs reflecting greater moisture and reduced insolation. Traders weigh these variables against typical climatological highs near 31 °C when assessing resolution probabilities.

These conditions favor daytime surface heating while boundary-layer moisture and minor timing differences in any weak frontal passage create the market’s clear tilt toward 30 °C (58 %) over 31 °C (30 %). Model spread remains modest, reflecting typical late-summer variability, with lower probabilities assigned to 29 °C or 32 °C tails. Updated ICON and ECMWF runs expected before evening will further constrain surface energy-balance projections ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast uncertainty for Tokyo’s August 14 maximum centers on expected cloud cover and scattered thunderstorms, which limit daytime heating and keep official readings clustered near 27–29 °C. Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models show a narrow range around these values, with precipitation probabilities of 30–40 % during peak heating hours reducing the chance of brief clear spells that could push readings to 30 °C or higher. Urban heat island effects and humidity levels near 80% further influence observed peaks, while historical analogs from similar synoptic patterns confirm reduced highs under overcast skies. Updated model runs and JMA briefings expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine resolution thresholds around these values.

Ensemble model guidance shows modest spread around 27–30°C depending on exact timing of any convective bursts, consistent with trader-implied odds clustering tightly at 27–29°C. Urban heat island effects and humidity levels near 80% further influence observed peaks, while historical analogs from similar synoptic patterns confirm reduced highs under overcast skies. Updated model runs and JMA briefings expected in the next 24–48 hours will likely refine resolution thresholds around these values.

eventMetadata.context_description: Stable high-pressure systems and limited cloud cover over southern Germany have positioned ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) for a Munich maximum of 29–31°C on August 12. Model consensus centers on 30°C as the most probable outcome, consistent with late-summer climatology where daily highs typically range 22–26°C but can reach the low 30s under clear anticyclonic conditions. Recent model runs show minimal spread, with only modest warming potential from daytime insolation and light winds, keeping 32°C or higher probabilities low. Traders have aligned closely with these official guidance updates, reflected in the dominant 30°C and 31°C shares.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Cloud cover and scattered showers are the dominant short-term factors capping Tokyo's August 14 maximum near 28–29°C according to Japan Meteorological Agency guidance.** Persistent moisture and limited solar insolation under mostly cloudy skies reduce surface heating compared with typical mid-August conditions under a strong Pacific High, which normally favors 31–34°C peaks. Ensemble forecasts show modest variability in shower timing and intensity that can shift the daily high by 1–2°C, keeping 27°C and 30°C outcomes plausible but less likely. The urban heat-island effect provides a small baseline boost, yet recent model runs emphasize the cooling influence of cloudiness over the next 48 hours. Updated JMA and global model guidance on August 13–14 will be the key catalysts for any further market movement.

eventMetadata.context_description: Stable high-pressure systems over central Europe have produced mostly sunny skies and light winds across Munich on August 12, 2026, supporting ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF and German Weather Service (DWD) that place the daytime maximum near 29–31 °C. Official observations and model consensus converge on 30 °C as the most probable peak, consistent with typical mid-August climatology for the region under clear anticyclonic conditions. Traders assign 92.5 % implied probability to this outcome because recent model runs show minimal spread and no significant cooling mechanisms such as increased cloud cover or frontal passage. A sudden increase in convective clouds or stronger northeasterly flow could cap temperatures at 28–29 °C, while unexpected clear-sky radiative heating might push readings to 31 °C, though both alternatives carry low market-implied odds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Stable high-pressure systems and limited cloud cover across southern Germany have positioned 30°C as the dominant outcome for Munich’s August 12 maximum, with ensemble runs from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) converging on a 29–31°C range and 30°C as the most frequent solution. The sharp probability drop beyond 31°C reflects model agreement that insufficient moisture or subsidence warming will limit further ascent, while sub-29°C scenarios remain low-probability given the established ridge and observed surface trends. Traders are monitoring the final afternoon model updates and any late-developing boundary-layer changes before resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Cloud cover and scattered showers are the dominant short-term factors capping Tokyo's August 14 maximum near 28–29°C according to Japan Meteorological Agency guidance.** Persistent moisture and limited solar insolation under mostly cloudy skies reduce surface heating compared with typical mid-August conditions under a strong Pacific High, which normally favors 31–34°C peaks. Ensemble forecasts show modest variability in shower timing and intensity that can shift the daily high by 1–2°C, keeping 27°C and 30°C outcomes plausible but less likely. The urban heat-island effect provides a small baseline boost, yet recent model runs emphasize the cooling influence of cloudiness over the next 48 hours. Updated JMA and global model guidance on August 13–14 will be the key catalysts for any further market movement.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) and Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) show strong model consensus around a 29–31°C maximum in Munich on August 12 under stable high-pressure conditions and limited cloud cover, driving the 96% market-implied probability for 30°C. These numerical weather prediction outputs incorporate surface observations, atmospheric soundings, and climatological baselines for mid-August, when typical highs range 23–26°C. Trader positioning reflects this convergence while acknowledging inherent forecast uncertainty from potential shifts in boundary-layer moisture or local advection. A sudden increase in convective cloudiness or stronger easterly flow could realistically lower the peak by 1–2°C, though current guidance offers limited support for such deviations before resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 13 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent high pressure, clear skies, and light winds are steering ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF and German Weather Service (DWD) toward a Munich maximum of 30–31 °C on August 13, producing the tight market split favoring the 31 °C outcome. These conditions favor strong daytime solar heating with minimal cloud cover or mixing, while typical late-summer climatology for southern Bavaria supports highs in this range absent stronger advection. Latest model runs show limited spread around these values, though minor shifts in boundary-layer moisture or timing of any weak frontal passage could still nudge the peak by 1 °C either way before tomorrow’s official observations finalize the result.

eventMetadata.context_description: High pressure dominating northwest Europe is driving the tight clustering of market-implied odds around 32–33 °C for London’s maximum on 14 August, with official Met Office guidance and ensemble runs showing a narrow range of outcomes under clear skies and light winds. Persistent anticyclonic conditions promote strong daytime insolation and minimal cloud cover, while elevated sea-surface temperatures around the UK reduce the usual maritime cooling effect and allow warmer air masses to advect from the continent. Model consensus places the peak near 31–34 °C, with small differences in boundary-layer mixing or slight timing of any weak frontal approach creating the spread that keeps 32 °C and 33 °C nearly tied. Updated short-range forecasts over the next 48 hours will determine whether the high edges toward the upper or lower side of this band.

Traders are monitoring the next DWD and ECMWF runs for any shifts in steering flow or boundary-layer moisture that could alter the outcome before resolution.

Updated short-range model runs from the JMA and ECMWF expected within the next 24–48 hours will likely refine the exact maximum before resolution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 14 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent JMA and global ensemble forecasts indicate a moderate Pacific high-pressure system dominating eastern Japan, with Tokyo expected to see highs near 28–29°C on August 14 amid increasing cloud cover and scattered showers that limit daytime heating. Model consensus shows modest uncertainty from variable steering flows and potential weak frontal passage, keeping probabilities clustered around 27–29°C rather than seasonal norms near 31°C. Urban heat island effects and high humidity will influence perceived conditions, though official resolution relies on JMA thermometer readings at the Tokyo station. Updated model runs and the next JMA three-day outlook, due within 24 hours, represent the next key catalysts for any shift in trader positioning.
